title: Cross-cultural regularities in the cognitive architecture of pride

findings.antecedent: 25 scenarios describing acts, traits, or circumstances
findings.consequent: valuation ratings by participants
findings.mechanism: widespread agreement on how valuation-enhancing these situations are relative to one another
findings.quote: mean intraclass correlation across the 16 countries: ICC (2,n) = 0.95

findings.antecedent: 25 scenarios describing acts, traits, or circumstances
findings.consequent: pride ratings by participants
findings.mechanism: Participants agree also about the extent to which they would feel pride in these situations
findings.quote: Participants agree also about the extent to which they would feel pride in these situations: mean ICC (2,n) = 0.92

findings.antecedent: mean valuation ratings for 25 scenarios
findings.consequent: mean pride ratings for 25 scenarios
findings.mechanism: Pride and valuation means are highly correlated with one another within each country
findings.quote: Pride and valuation means are highly correlated with one another within each country, with a mean r = 0.82

findings.antecedent: mean valuation ratings for 24 scenarios (excluding scenario 11)
findings.consequent: mean pride ratings for 24 scenarios (excluding scenario 11)
findings.mechanism: Excluding this scenario from analysis does not substantially change the pride-valuation correlations
findings.quote: mean r = 0.77 (SD = 0.09; minimum r = 0.55; maximum r = 0.88; N r values = 16); P values = 10−7–0.005

findings.antecedent: 25 scenarios
findings.consequent: mean valuation ratings across countries
findings.mechanism: high degree of between-country agreement on the extent to which a given situation would elicit positive valuation
findings.quote: mean r = 0.90 (SD = 0.06; minimum r = 0.73; maximum r = 0.98; N r values = 120); P values = 10−17–10−4

findings.antecedent: 25 scenarios
findings.consequent: mean pride ratings across countries
findings.mechanism: high degree of between-country agreement on the extent to which a given situation would elicit pride
findings.quote: mean r = 0.81 (SD = 0.11; minimum r = 0.51; maximum r = 0.97; N r values = 120); P values = 10−14–0.009

findings.antecedent: mean valuation ratings from other 15 countries for 25 scenarios
findings.consequent: mean pride ratings in a given country for 25 scenarios
findings.mechanism: the pride elicited in each of the 16 countries is positively correlated with the valuations from the other 15 countries
findings.quote: mean r = 0.75 (SD = 0.09; minimum r = 0.48; maximum r = 0.93; N r values = 240); P values = 10−10–0.017

findings.antecedent: mean valuation ratings from other 15 countries for 24 scenarios (excluding scenario 11)
findings.consequent: mean pride ratings in a given country for 24 scenarios (excluding scenario 11)
findings.mechanism: Excluding scenario 11 from analysis does not substantially alter the between-country pride-valuation correlations
findings.quote: mean r = 0.69 (SD = 0.13; minimum r = 0.29; maximum r = 0.90; N r values = 240); P values = 10−8–0.17
